request.system:
You are an extraction engine for transcripts of the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central launch event videos.
You read machine-generated captions that carry a timestamp (seconds) per segment and you return structured JSON.

Hard rules:
- Use only what the transcript says. Do not add product knowledge, context or guesses from outside the transcript.
- Every timestamp you return must be a segment start time "t" that exists in the input, or lie inside a segment's range. Never invent timestamps.
- Quotes must be verbatim substrings of a segment text (same words, same order; you may trim the start and end). 8 to 25 words each. No paraphrasing, no fixing grammar, no stitching segments.
- Status is only what is said or shown in this video: "preview" if they say preview, public preview, beta or similar; "ga" if they say generally available, GA, out of preview, released; "announced" if it is mentioned as coming later, not in this release, roadmap; "unclear" if nothing is said. Always give the quote that proves the status, or null.
- Names of presenters are "as heard"; mark confidence low when the captions could have mangled them.
- No em-dashes anywhere in your text. Use a plain hyphen.
- Write summaries in plain language, no hype words copied from the video (no "exciting", "powerful", "seamless").

output.summary: The video introduces the Subcontracting app for Business Central, which was quietly released in minor update three and is now pre-installed on new environments. Existing environments can install it from Marketplace, AppSource or from the legacy Subcontracting worksheet. The demo follows one order through the flow: the component supply method on BOM lines, production order components and routing, the subcontracting purchase order, comments and attachments, and transfer orders with WIP items and a WIP ledger entry. It then covers item charge assignment to receipts, closest-match subcontractor pricing with a minimum amount, and receiving through warehouse receipts and inventory put-away with serial numbers. Almost no preview or GA labels are given, apart from a remark that one warehouse scenario already existed in minor release 28.3.

chapters.title: Intro and what the Subcontracting app covers
How to get the Subcontracting app
Component supply method on the bill of material
Production order components and routing fact box
Comments, attachments and the transfer WIP item on the routing
Transfer order to subcontractor and WIP ledger entry
Receipt, item charge assignment and cost recap
Warehouse receipt with serial numbers (directed put-away)
Inventory put-away on a basic location and wrap-up

features.name: Subcontracting app (re-introduction)
features.description: A Subcontracting app that was silently released in minor update three but not pre-installed. It is now pre-installed on new environments in the latest version and extends the older, limited subcontracting that only registered that the work happened.
features.status_evidence_quote: we are silently released it in minor update three
caveats: Was not pre-installed on new or upgraded environments when first released
Upgraded environments need to install it themselves

features.name: Installing the Subcontracting app
features.description: Upgraded environments can install the app from Microsoft Marketplace, from the AppSource list inside Business Central, or directly from a notification on the existing Subcontracting worksheet, which the app replaces.
features.status_evidence_quote: for new environments in the latest version, you will get up pre-installed
caveats: The install was not actually performed in the demo
prerequisites: Upgraded environment from a previous version

features.name: Legacy Subcontracting worksheet replacement
features.description: The Subcontracting app will replace the legacy Subcontracting worksheet. Opening the worksheet shows a notification with an install action.

features.name: Subcontracting assisted setup
features.description: An assisted setup that fills in default values automatically, lets you change them, and links to other subcontracting-related pages.

features.name: Warehouse handling, price management and cost allocation for subcontracting
features.description: Subcontracting operations can use the standard warehouse processes. The speakers also mention more price management and extra ability to allocate cost, to be shown in later demos.
caveats: Only previewed as a topic in this window

features.name: Component supply method on BOM lines
features.description: A new field on production bill of material lines sets how each component reaches the subcontractor: transferred from your location by transfer order, consignment at vendor (bought straight to the vendor location), or vendor supplied (bought from that vendor and consumed in the finished good cost).

features.name: Subcontracting components on the production order
features.description: On a refreshed released production order, components linked to the subcontracting operation get different location codes. Transfer components point to the main location, and the others point to the location set on the vendor card.

features.name: Vendor card field for components at vendor location
features.description: A new field on the vendor card tracks components that are still owned by the company but sit at the vendor location. It shows consignment and vendor supplied components.

features.name: Subcontracting fact box on routing
features.description: A new fact box on production order routing shows whether a line is a subcontracting operation and details such as the connected components, linked through the routing link code.

features.name: Create subcontracting order from production order routing
features.description: A subcontracting purchase order can be created directly from the production order routing with one action. The worksheet is still available for bulk operations with extra capabilities.

features.name: Subcontracting purchase order lines
features.description: The generated purchase order holds a line for the vendor-supplied component bought to the subcontractor location, an item line for the routing operation, an info line with the production order line description, and comment lines with instructions for the subcontractor.
caveats: Demo data was changed to include two subcontractors linked to work centers and locations

features.name: Manufacturing setup: subcontracting FastTab
features.description: Manufacturing setup gets a Subcontracting FastTab. The toggle Create production order info line adds a comment line with the production order line description. A component transfer lead time field (one day in the demo) is used later.
caveats: The lead time field is only introduced, its use comes later

features.name: Subcontracting details fact box on purchase lines
features.description: A fact box on the purchase order line shows the connected production order, with links to the production order, transfer orders, routings and components.

features.name: Subcontracting comments on routing
features.description: Routing lines get a subcontracting comment that is copied to the purchase order. It can be edited on the production order routing lines or inherited from standard tasks.

features.name: Attachments flowing from routing to production order and purchase order
features.description: Attachments on routing have two toggles, flow to production order and flow to purchase, so a subcontracting description document is copied to the purchase order. Attachments are shown per line, not on the document header.
caveats: Header attachments stay empty because one purchase order can cover several production orders or lines
prerequisites: Attachment on the routing with the flow toggles enabled

features.name: Transfer WIP item and WIP ledger entry
features.description: A routing line can be marked with a transfer WIP item, so work-in-progress goods that are not finished goods can be tracked when moved to and from the subcontractor. Posting the transfer does not create item ledger entries for that line but registers a new work in progress ledger entry.
caveats: Makes little sense for the first operation, since nothing is work in progress yet
prerequisites: Subcontracting not as the first operation, for a meaningful WIP item
WIP item defined on the routing line

features.name: Create transfer order to subcontractor
features.description: A Subcontracting action under Functions on the production order creates a transfer order from the main location to the subcontractor location. It holds one line for the component to transfer and one line for the transfer WIP item.
caveats: The action can be personalized if you use subcontracting a lot
prerequisites: Components with the transfer supply method
Production BOM component set to be transferred from own location

features.name: Subcontracting details fact box with WIP quantity
features.description: A fact box on the production order routing shows the WIP quantity at the subcontractor and allows drill-down to the WIP ledger entries. This shows how much must be transferred back, and fact boxes and actions link purchase, transfer and production orders.

features.name: Item charge assignment to subcontracting receipt lines
features.description: Item charges can be assigned to posted purchase receipt lines of a subcontracting order, including the operation line. The production order statistics then show the charge in actual subcontractor cost.
caveats: Actual cost only shows the item charges because the vendor invoice was not posted in the demo
prerequisites: Purchase invoice with an item charge line

features.name: Subcontractor prices with closest match
features.description: Subcontractor prices are matched by closest match on quantity, date, task, unit of measure and variant, not by the lowest price as in normal purchase pricing. A larger order can therefore get a higher unit price if the vendor price list says so.
caveats: Differs from standard purchase price logic, which picks the best price
prerequisites: Subcontractor prices defined on the item

features.name: Standard task codes
features.description: Standard task codes are now included in Dynamics 365 to make it easier to demonstrate different subcontractor pricing. They were not used in the demo.

features.name: Minimum amount per line for subcontractor price
features.description: If the line amount is below the vendor minimum amount, the price becomes the minimum amount divided by the quantity. In the demo, a minimum of 100 and quantity 2 gives a unit price of 50.
prerequisites: Minimum amount set on the subcontractor price

features.name: Subcontracting with warehouse receipt and item tracking (directed put-away)
features.description: For a white location with directed put-away, a subcontracting order needs a warehouse receipt. Serial numbers can be assigned and put-away created only when it is the last operation, otherwise the receipt registers the production output. The speaker says this was already in minor release 28.3.
features.status_evidence_quote: that's not something like very, very new because we already had it in minor release 28.3.
caveats: Serial numbers and put-away only for the last operation
prerequisites: Location with directed put-away and pick (white location)

features.name: Subcontracting with inventory put-away on a basic location
features.description: On a location that requires put-away and pick but has no warehouse receipt or shipment, the subcontracting order can be received through an inventory put-away. Serial numbers can be assigned there and quantity to handle can be auto filled.
caveats: Presenter wishes the convenient assign function also existed on this page
prerequisites: Location requiring put-away and pick without warehouse receipt or shipment

features.name: Serial numbers defined at any level in subcontracting
features.description: Serial numbers can be defined on the production order and copied to the purchase order, or defined on the purchase document and used to populate the inventory put-away. Any receiving method works: purchase document, warehouse receipt or inventory put-away.
caveats: Lot numbers were not demoed, the speaker says they work the same
